note: The Dalton Data Bank index, adjudicated against the town. Written here rather than into data/research/census_1840/crosswalk.json because that file is generated by tools/crosswalk_census_1840_heads.py --build and a hand edit would be overwritten. Same shape and same rules as data/research/newspapers/identity.json: a merge needs a rule, the rule names BOTH spellings verbatim, a surname-only merge is always a refusal, and a candidate is neither a merge nor a refusal.

passes.what: the 20 rows of the index's 1840 Illinois census block, adjudicated against the residents layer, the 1833-1835 voter and poll lists, and PR #670's 210 named 1840 heads
passes.why_twelve_are_not_adjudicated: Twelve rows name Morgan, Knox, Pike, Adams, Scott and Jo Daviess counties. They are recorded so the Chicago selection is made from a declared whole, and they meet nothing in this town — there is no pair to rule on.

refusals.rule: 'Mr. Dalton' of the index's 1840 entry 15 (Cook Co., 1 Ward Chicago) is NOT 'Edward Dalton' of hh_dalton_edward: the index prints a courtesy title and no given name, and a surname-only row can never carry an identity here however well the place agrees. It stands in the same First Ward as entry 3, which is why it matters: it makes the ward a shared address rather than a discriminator.

'Mike Dalton' (entry 13, Cook Co.) is not merged with 'Michael Dalton' (entry 14, 2 Ward, Chicago): the index prints them as two separate rows in one alphabetical block and supplies nothing — no page, no line, no household — that either joins or separates them. The familiar-for-formal pair is a clue and this project has never accepted one as an identity.
'Michael Dalton' of the index's 1840 entry 14 (2 Ward, Chicago) is NOT 'Edward Dalton' of hh_dalton_edward: the given names disagree outright, and the town holds no Michael Dalton.
'Mike Dalton' of the index's 1840 entry 13 (Cook Co.) is NOT 'Edward Dalton' of hh_dalton_edward: the given names disagree, and the row names no place inside the town.

'George Dalton' of the index's 1840 entry 4 (Cook County, Thornton Precinct) is NOT 'Edward Dalton' of hh_dalton_edward: the given names disagree, and Thornton Precinct is southern Cook County some twenty miles from the town.
'Gerard Dalton' of the index's 1840 entry 6 (Cook Co) is NOT 'Edward Dalton' of hh_dalton_edward: the given names disagree, and the row names no place at all inside the county.

'Patrick Dalton' of the index's 1840 entry 16 (Cook Co., Bridgeport) is NOT 'Edward Dalton' of hh_dalton_edward: the given names disagree, and Bridgeport is the canal terminus outside the 1835 town plat.

candidates.status: unchanged — retained exactly as T-0479 left it, and QUALIFIED
candidates.basis: Exact given name and surname, in Chicago, five years after the 1835 postal return.
candidates.qualification_added_by_this_pass: T-0479 read this row as an Edward Dalton in Chicago's First Ward and treated that ward as part of the agreement. The whole 1840 block, read now, carries a SECOND First-Ward Dalton household — 'Mr. Dalton, Cook Co., 1 Ward Chicago' — and a third Dalton household in the Second Ward. So the ward locates a name among at least two Dalton households, and cannot itself narrow anything. The candidate is no weaker in its name agreement and no stronger in its place agreement than it was; it is simply not unique in its ward, and the reading that made it did not know that.
conflicts: Index-only access path: no page, no line, no household composition, and no route back to the sheet.
A second First-Ward Dalton household stands in the same index block (entry 15).
Five years and no occupation, address, family or continuity bridge between the 1835 letter list and the 1840 enumeration.
